title: Sportking India Ltd - 539221 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Sportking Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin reached about 18.8% on yarn spreads of INR133/kg versus INR107 last quarter, with management guiding 18-20% margins to be hard to sustain.
summary.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as a strong start, with healthy revenue growth and a significant profitability improvement driven by better cotton yarn realisations, strong export demand and disciplined raw material buying. The overall spread rose to INR133/kg from INR107 in the prior quarter, and the EBITDA margin was cited at about 18.8%. Management said the margin is elevated, expects the next two quarters to stay around these levels, and expects longer-term margins near 15% after the Odisha plant. The solar project started commercial operations late in the prior quarter (about 10 days of contribution) and is guided to save about INR15 crore a year, with the full 90 days flowing from the current month.

segments.name: Cotton yarn
segments.commentary: Better realisations cited as main driver of margin expansion; spread rose to INR133/kg from INR107/kg. Management said the Odisha plant will add to revenue from Q4.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Management targets a 55:45 export-to-domestic split. China and Bangladesh together account for about 60-70% of Sportking's exports; China's incremental yarn demand was the main driver of the recent uptick.

segments.name: Fabric and garments (proposed acquisitions)
segments.commentary: Proposed acquisitions of Marvel Dyers and Sobhagia Sales are expected to add 8-10% to top line and similar EBITDA share from next year, with about INR250 crore impact from next financial year once the deal completes.

capex_capacity: Greenfield 150,000-spindle expansion in Odisha: first-phase production expected in Q3 FY27, full project targeted within FY27; announced cost about INR975-1,000 crore.
Management expects 30-40% of potential revenue from the new plant in Q4 FY27 and targets 90% plant utilisation by March 2027 and 96-97% by the start of FY28; ramp-up expected to take 5-6 months.
Odisha margins expected at least 300-400 bps above existing plants, per management.
Odisha incentives: INR2.50/unit power subsidy, 30% capital subsidy with no cap, land subsidy tied to employment, and about INR7,000 per employee employment subsidy.
Land is available to triple Odisha capacity; further capex depends on balance sheet and leverage comfort.
Solar project commissioned and operating; expected to cut annual power cost by 12-15%.
demand_pricing: Management said demand from all markets remains healthy and expects festive-season support domestically.

Global cotton yarn demand improved as China became a large buyer, pushing Indian yarn prices higher; management said China imports about 20,000 tonnes against India's roughly 400,000 tonnes monthly output.
Order book kept at 70-90 days, similar to end of last quarter.
Cotton prices rose about 10-11% over the last quarter; management says most purchases were made about 3 months earlier and that Q2 should be similar to or better than Q1.
India-UK FTA signed last month, but no orders yet; management expects 6-9 months for orders to reflect in the order book.

Management expects China to remain a buyer because Chinese cotton prices are above international levels. Bangladesh's spinning sector is under strain from gas and capital costs, which helps Indian yarn demand.
Exports to the US are indirect via downstream vendors whose offtake has roughly doubled in the last 6 months.
guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin expected around 18-19% for the next two quarters; longer-term margin guided around 15% after Odisha, with 12-14% described as the comfortable range.
FY27 revenue target about INR3,000 crore (around 20% growth); FY28 target above INR4,000 crore with Odisha.
Solar savings about INR15 crore annually; full 90-day contribution expected from the current month.
Absolute EBITDA expected to keep rising in FY28 even if percentage margins moderate.
Cotton import duty waiver runs to 31 October; management is lobbying the government to extend it and says FY27 inventory is already covered for two quarters.
Acquisition completion expected in about one more quarter, with full impact from next financial year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA margin sustainability and what drove the 18.8% margin, including the import duty effect?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the cotton import duty made no contribution to Q1 because raw material was already bought; margins should stay around current levels for two quarters, with absolute EBITDA expected to keep trending higher.

qa_highlights.question: Is the spread of INR133/kg sustainable for a year or two?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to predict precisely, expects cotton prices to ease after the new crop, and said the inventory effect will be larger in the next two quarters because Q1 realisations lagged cotton prices.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Odisha plant reach high utilisation and what is the revenue run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 96-97% utilisation by start of FY28; no Q3 revenue assumed, with 30-40% of potential revenue from Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the merger financing and debt position?
qa_highlights.answer: Mostly preferential shares, with cash outflow of about INR25-30 crore and no meaningful incremental debt.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company add capacity beyond Odisha Phase 1?
qa_highlights.answer: Land exists to triple Odisha capacity; further capex depends on the balance sheet and leverage comfort.

qa_highlights.question: What is the long-term product mix shift toward value-added products?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said value-added fabric and garment share would be about 10% in the next year; longer-term plans to be announced once there is more visibility.

risks_watch: Cyclicality: management itself flagged 18-20% margins as likely not sustainable long term and cited FY22 peaks as an aberration.
Cotton input cost: prices up 10-11% in the last quarter; management expects a moderation after October, but the import duty waiver ends on 31 October unless extended.
Capacity additions: spread strength may attract new spindle capacity; management says it has not seen announced projects.
Odisha ramp-up: 5-6 month ramp, targeted 90% utilisation by March 2027, and margin accretion (300-400 bps) depend on execution.
Acquisitions of Marvel Dyers and Sobhagia Sales: completion timing has slipped and the contribution is still under progress.
Export concentration: China and Bangladesh make up 60-70% of exports; the China-driven demand could reverse.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on demand, margins and the Odisha plant, but guarded on forward cotton and spread outlook, with repeated statements that it is difficult to predict. Evasive on pricing details, declining to share cotton cost or realisation numbers.
key_quotes: So the overall spread was INR133 vis-a-vis INR107 last quarter.
And the 18%, 19%, 20% might not be sustainable in the long-term, but we expect them to be healthier than where they were in last 2, 3 years going forward next year.
So I won't take it as a benchmark for the volatility of margins. Otherwise, they stay between 12% to 14%, which is where we are comfortable actually.

growth.why: Management guides FY27 revenue to about INR3,000 crore (~20% growth from ~INR2,500 crore), backed by the 150,000-spindle Odisha plant (first phase Q3 FY27, 30-40% of potential revenue in Q4, 90% utilisation by March 2027), a 70-90 day order book and China/Bangladesh export demand; quarterly revenue and EBITDA growth YoY were not stated.
